risks.note: The auditor carries an Emphasis of Matter on Note 41: a cyber security incident on 18 February 2026 caused loss of the back-up of books of account for 01 April 2025 to 18 February 2026. Data for 01 April 2025 to 29 September 2025 was restored from software back-up, but data for 30 September 2025 to 18 February 2026 was 'reconstructed and re-entered in the books of account based on available supporting records and documentation'. The Board's Report describes the incident as impacting account-related data from 01 October 2025 onwards, with affected systems isolated and 'a comprehensive investigation currently in progress' - i.e. still unresolved at the date of the report. This is the single most concrete company-specific risk in the annual report, and it goes to the reliability of a full quarter and a half of reported numbers.
risks.risk: Cyber incident that destroyed the books-of-account backup, forcing part of the year's accounting data to be reconstructed by hand

risks.note: Books are maintained on accounting software operated and managed by a third-party service provider. In the absence of audit-trail details in the Service Organization Controls report, the auditor was 'unable to comment on whether audit trail feature of the said software were enabled and operated throughout the year... or whether there were any instances of the audit trail feature being tampered with', and after the cyber incident could not obtain sufficient appropriate evidence that the audit trail was preserved per Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014. The auditor also could not comment on compliance with the daily back-up requirement for the affected period. Outsourced accounting infrastructure is therefore a live control weakness, not a resolved one.
risks.risk: Audit-trail / IT-control qualification the auditor could not clear

risks.note: MD&A flags 'Supply Chain and Manufacturing Risks: Raw material availability, quality control, and third-party manufacturing dependency can impact operations.' Amwill owns no plant - the Board's Report confirms it is not engaged in any manufacturing activity - so every product's quality, cost, capacity and regulatory standing sits with partners it does not control, and a partner failure translates directly into stock-outs or product-quality events.
risks.risk: Total dependence on third-party contract manufacturers

risks.note: MD&A flags 'stringent product approval requirements, evolving health and safety regulations, and restrictions on marketing claims necessitat[ing] continuous compliance vigilance'. For a business whose entire proposition is clinically-validated efficacy, restrictions on what can be claimed constrain the marketing model itself, not just the paperwork.
risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance exposure in a claims-sensitive category

risks.note: MD&A flags 'Risks of adverse reactions, long-term side effects, and challenges in clinical validation [that] require robust quality assurance and pharmacovigilance systems.' The portfolio includes prescription-grade actives (steroids, antifungals, minoxidil-finasteride combinations), where an adverse-event cluster would carry both regulatory and reputational consequences.
risks.risk: Product safety and efficacy / pharmacovigilance risk

risks.note: MD&A flags 'Intense competition, shifting consumer preferences, and pricing pressures persist across the dermo cosmetic segment', and separately notes the dermatology segment is 'attracting significant strategic and private equity interest' with 'leading players accelerating new product launches' - i.e. the same growth that draws Amwill is drawing far better-capitalised entrants.
risks.risk: Intense competition and pricing pressure in dermo-cosmetics

risks.note: MD&A flags 'Consumer trust is paramount; social media influence amplifies both positive and negative perceptions.' For a dermatologist-recommended brand whose moat is prescriber trust, a viral safety or efficacy complaint can damage the prescription channel faster than any distribution advantage can repair it.
risks.risk: Reputational risk amplified by social media

risks.note: MD&A flags 'Patent protection and ensuring adequate returns on R&D investment remain ongoing concerns.' In a private-label model where formulations are developed with and by manufacturing partners, protecting differentiation is structurally harder, and formulations can be replicated by competitors using the same contract manufacturers.
